top.title: Jupiter swimming and diving wins first-ever state championship
top.description: Jupiter boys swimming and diving has completed its "dream" season with the most coveted of state hardware. The Warriors' program won its first-ever state championship, pacing the pool across Class 4A to finish first at the podium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Jupiter outlasted runner-up Cypress Bay by 5.5 points to take home gold, with the competition coming down to the very last event. The Warriors team swam the 400 yard relay with a time of 3:01.30, edging the second-place Lightning in the event as well as the total team score. "It was an incredible, historical moment for Jupiter High School because this is the first time we're winning the championship title with the boys," head coach Kiril Zahariev said. Jupiter paced the field with 206.5 points, followed by Cypress Bay with 201, Winter Park with 186.5, Nease with 153, and Riverview Sarasota with 143 to round out Florida's top five across Class 4A. FHSAA football playoff bracket release: 5 Palm Beach County takeaways Wellington transfer Julian Granison and Charles "Buddy" Howard shared the honors of "MBS" as Zahariev puts it ― "most valuable swimmer." Granison, a Florida commit, won the 50-yard (19.50, a personal best) and 100-yard frees (42.86, a personal best) events, while Howard, a Michigan commit, took first place in the 200-yard free (1:36.70, a personal best) and 100-yard fly (48.15) events. Chase Young and Asher Smith also participated in the winning 400-yard free relay team, while Slater Woodard helped the Warriors win the 200 free relay. The Warriors boys program boasted six seniors this season, with all coming together to finish their respective high school careers on top with the state title. "It was an amazing performance by all the kids," Zahariev said. "We are so blessed with the title." On the Jupiter girls' side, NC State commit Veronica Metz won the 200 free in a time of 1:45.68, helping the Warriors to a fourth-place finish. Boca Raton junior Caleb Caponera also shined for the Bobcats' boys program with two titles. He swam a 1:46.57 in the 200 IM and a 55.71 in the 100 breast. Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@usatodayco.com. top.title: Cardinals get brutal season-ending news on Michael Wilson amid neck fracture
top.description: Cardinals get brutal season-ending news on Michael Wilson amid neck fracture originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals have three wins in the 2026 NFL season, and aren't exactly playing great football. But part of the issue has been some horrible injury luck. Jeremiyah Love has missed a big chunk of the season, and they've also seen a few key linemen miss time. Kendrick Bourne is out for the season, and unfortunately, the hits keep coming for the Cardinals. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Michael Wilson is now out for the rest of the season after suffering a neck injury against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9. Michael Wilson out for rest of 2026 after neck injury "Sources: AZCardinals WR Michael Wilson is out for the season after suffering a neck injury. Brutal," Rapoport reported. Not long after Rapoport's report, Cardinals' head coach Mike LaFleur revealed some shocking news about the neck injury. According to Josh Weinfuss of ESPN, the context of Wilson's neck injury makes it a lot more brutal for the WR. Not only was it a neck fracture, which is a scary-sounding injury, but Wilson actually suffered the injury on the fourth play of the game, didn't tell anyone, and played through a fractured neck for almost the entirety of the team's Week 9 loss. Wilson suffered a fractured neck on the fourth play of the game and wound up playing the remainder of the game for the Cardinals in an incredibly gutsy performance. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Of course, considering that this is a likely lost season for the Cardinals anyway, there is zero reason to try and bring Wilson back this season. After the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, and both of the season-ending injuries to Wilson and Bourne, the Cardinals are now down to just Reggie Vergil, Simi Fehoko, Harrison Wallace III, and Devin Duvernay in their WR room. It would not be a surprise if the Cardinals made a move for some WR help, as their injuries have piled up to a ridiculous degree. Wilson will now miss the remainder of the season with a neck fracture that he initially played through. It's a brutal injury for the new $75 million WR. The next time the Cardinals see him, it will be in 2027, potentially with another new quarterback. top.description: Enzo Maresca's side lost their third consecutive Premier League game on Saturday -Credit:Lexy Ilsley, Manchester City FC via Getty Images Manchester City have been dealt another injury setback after Abdukodir Khusanov picked up a problem in the 3-1 loss to Nottingham Forest. The center-back finished the game at the City Ground but will miss Uzbekistan's upcoming friendlies against Russia and Saudi Arabia. The severity of Khusanov's injury remains unclear, but it adds to manager Enzo Maresca's concerns after two additional defenders requested substitutions at Forest. Marc Guéhi and Joško Gvardiol both experienced issues that led to their half-time withdrawals, while Nico O'Reilly has been omitted from the latest England squad after failing to reach full fitness throughout the season. Guéhi has subsequently withdrawn from the England squad, with Newcastle United's Dan Burn called up in his place. Meanwhile, it's uncertain whether Gvardiol will also pull out of Croatia duty, but Maresca must find stability at the back. City suffered their third consecutive Premier League defeat with the loss at Forest - following losses to Brighton and Hove Albion and Aston Villa - to enter the latest international window on a disappointing note. Jair Cunha opened the scoring for Forest within six minutes, pouncing as Gvardiol was caught on the ball, with Liam Delap doubling their lead shortly after with a thundering run and shot. Rayan Cherki brought City back into the match with a top corner half-volley in the 52nd minute, before Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap combined to put the nail in the coffin via a deadly counter-attack with less than 20 minutes to go. Maresca acknowledged his team requires recovery time as he attempts to diagnose their slump in form before they resume action against Fulham a week on Saturday. top.title: Red Wings Playing Things Down to the Wire with Edvinsson
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Defenseman Simon Edvinsson remains unsigned through the first week of November, and the second month of the NHL season as the Detroit Red Wings find themselves floundering after a Halloween loss that seems to continue to haunt the team. The Red Wings could certainly use the big Swedish defenseman as they find themselves with a difficult schedule ahead against top Atlantic teams including the Florida Panthers, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Boston Bruins. For the moment, however, Edvinsson is still renting ice time in Nashville at the Predators’ facilities. Well, Simon Edvinsson is still here. pic.twitter.com/dc2SIkUZkY — Alex Daugherty (@AlexDaugherty1) November 9, 2026 According to the Lower Broad’s Nick Kieser, who met with Edvinsson in an unofficial capacity, Edvinsson came to the music city after Predators’ forward Filip Forsberg recommended a local skating coach, and “hopes to get something done soon.” Staring contest So far in the month and a half or so of Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff’ s tenure there has not appeared to be much movement in getting Edvinsson re-signed after the team failed to negotiate a contract for him before the end of training camp. On Oct. 30 TSN’s Darren Dreger reported that the Red Wings have submitted several contract offers to the Swedish blueliner at a variety of term lengths, but with the defenseman still skating in Nashville over the last week, it appears that progress towards pen to paper has stalled out. Insider Elliotte Friedman stated on a Friday appearance on NHL Now that Edvinsson was adamant about not wanting to play again in Detroit, however, that the Red Wings were willing to wait down until the Dec. 1 deadline to see if a deal can be done, much like Toronto did several years ago with William Nylander . “Right now there’s a lot of people who seem to think that the Red Wings will, if they want, if the Red Wings feel that ‘if we have to test him to see if his resolve is real’, they’ll do it.” Friedman said. Interestingly, the Predators will be visiting the Red Wings at home for Detroit’s last game of the month on Nov. 28 , two days before the Dec. 1 deadline to sign the defenseman for the season. Horcoff and the rest of the Detroit brass have been reportedly fending off potential trade partners with an exorbitant trade acquisition cost for Edvinsson in the meanwhile as they work to bring him back into the fold. top.title: Bob Nightengale just asking questions about possible Fernando Tatis Jr., Mason Miller trades
top.description: Denis Poroy-Imagn Images Bob Nightengale just asking questions about possible Fernando Tatis Jr., Mason Miller trades appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Diego Padres could face difficult decisions this offseason as their new ownership group evaluates the franchise’s financial future. With several major contracts on the books and key players potentially attracting interest , trade speculation is beginning to surround Fernando Tatis Jr. and Mason Miller . In his latest USA Today column, Bob Nightengale discussed the uncertainty facing MLB teams ahead of a potential lockout and the possibility of more aggressive trade activity. Nightengale noted that executives would look to “coerce rivals into trades” during the general manager meetings. While that does not confirm the Padres are shopping either player, it has added to questions about how A.J. Preller could reshape the roster. Fernando Tatis Jr . would be a particularly difficult player to move. The 27-year-old remains one of baseball’s most dynamic talents, combining power, speed and defensive versatility. He also has eight years and approximately $266 million remaining on his contract, along with a full no-trade clause through 2028. Any potential deal would require his approval and a significant return for San Diego. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mason Miller could also attract attention after establishing himself as one of the game’s premier relief pitchers. He recorded 38 saves and 129 strikeouts in 2026, making him a valuable asset for a contender seeking late-inning help. The Padres would likely demand a substantial prospect package before considering such a move. The St. Louis Cardinals could emerge as an intriguing hypothetical destination for Tatis. His father, Fernando Tatis Sr., previously played for St. Louis, while the Cardinals have young talent and financial flexibility to explore a major acquisition. However, there is no confirmed link between the two sides. For now, the Padres’ plans remain unclear. Any decision involving Tatis or Miller would depend on the new ownership group’s direction and Preller’s assessment of the team’s future. top.description: Michigan State’s path to bowl eligibility now comes down to three games. The Spartans sit at 3-6 and have to win all three to get to the six wins a bowl requires, starting Saturday at home against Washington, with No. 23 Oregon and Rutgers after that. That math only exists because of Saturday night in Ann Arbor. After Michigan State beat Michigan 15-6, bringing Paul Bunyan back to East Lansing for the first time since 2021 , the Spartans snapped a six-game losing streak and gave themselves something to play for in November. Pat Fitzgerald spoke to the media Monday in a video posted by Spartan Mag about where that bowl goal sits. Michigan State Bowl Eligibility Starts With Washington Fitzgerald did not spend long on the big picture, and he did not pretend it was not there either. “Talked about the macro for about eight seconds this morning in a team meeting, and close that drawer up pretty quickly, but I like having motivation in November,” Fitzgerald said. He was more direct about what the three games could buy his roster. “There’s no doubt there’s an opportunity if we do what we’re capable of to create an extra month with our seniors,” Fitzgerald said, per the Detroit News . Bowl eligibility would be Michigan State’s first since 2021. For now, his message to the team stops at Washington. “We all know that, that win you know gave us an opportunity, and the right to have this be a big game this weekend,” Fitzgerald said. “That’s the way I’ve approached it with the guys, this is a critical game for this team. You know I said, listen, then that creates next week and the week after; we’ll worry about them down the road.” The Players Proved They Could Execute The Game Plan Pat Fitzgerald said his players came to him to point out their mistakes after the 28-10 loss to UCLA , and they used the bye week to lock back in. top.title: Jets’ Scott Arniel reveals ‘hard’ part of Connor Hellebuyck not starting in Devils clash
top.description: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Jets’ Scott Arniel reveals ‘hard’ part of Connor Hellebuyck not starting in Devils clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Winnipeg Jets will welcome the New Jersey Devils to Canada Life Centre on Tuesday night for the first time since the Connor Hellebuyck trade — but almost inexplicably, the 33-year-old will not be between the pipes for the contest. Instead, the Devils will turn to Jake Allen, while Hellebuyck , who spent the first 11 years of his career in Manitoba, will watch from the bench. The decision has drawn sharp criticism from across the hockey world, and Jets head coach Scott Arniel chimed in on Monday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It goes back to the ownership, it goes back to the fans, it goes back to the core guys that have been with Helly from the very beginning, who he kind of left on,” the bench boss told reporters, per TSN. “That’s the part for me that’s hard, he just gave up on us, and so it would be nice to just finally be done with this. All it does is drag it out 10 or nine more games from now, we’re going to have to start into it and talk about it again here. That’s the biggest disappointment.” Jets head coach Scott Arniel shares his thoughts on Connor Hellebuyck not starting in his return to Winnipeg. pic.twitter.com/fSBrsqTvRl — TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 9, 2026 The Jets and Devils will play for the second and final time in 2026-27 on Nov. 28 in Newark. New Jersey general manager Sunny Mehta announced the decision Sunday, and Hellebuyck also shared his thoughts , saying he was disappointed he wouldn’t be starting. “We definitely had a conversation and I told them my thoughts on it and they told me theirs, and at the end of the day I have to listen to them and I can only push so hard,” Hellebuyck said. “I can only push so hard. I was adamant that I want to play, but it is what it is.” Mehta said that starting Hellebuyck on Tuesday “would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability,” an explanation that has drawn widespread criticism . Hellebuyck is 5-0-0 with a 1.96 goals-against average and .913 save percentage with the Devils, and he just shut out the Toronto Maple Leafs on Sunday. Meanwhile, Allen sports a 3.20 goals-against average and .881 save percentage. It’s a bad look for the Devils, who should have let Hellebuyck face the music and move on. Instead, they’ve prolonged the storyline until the teams meet again at the end of the month — with no guarantee he’ll start that game, either.

top.title: St. Louis Cardinals Interested in Reunion With World Series Champion
top.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - JULY 6: Oliver Marmol #37 of the St. Louis Cardinals looks on prior to the game against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on July 6, 2023 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Sam Navarro/Getty Images) Getty The St. Louis Cardinals traded away starter Dustin May and reliever JoJo Romero to the Milwaukee Brewers at the Trade Deadline in a fire sale. Those two players would win a World Series with Milwaukee, becoming key contributors. Now, both will hit free agency. May’s market is likely cold after how he finished the year, but Romero’s could be hot. According to Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Dispatch, the Cardinals are considering a reunion with Romero. The left-handed reliever recorded a 3.36 ERA in 2026 between St. Louis and Milwaukee. Should The Cardinals Bring Back Romero? The Philadelphia Phillies drafted Romero in the fourth round of the 2016 MLB Draft out of Yavapai College. He debuted with Philadelphia during the COVID-shortened 2020 season with horrible results. In 25 games over three seasons with the Phillies, Romero recorded a 7.89 ERA. Philadelphia traded him to St. Louis in exchange for utility man Edmundo Sosa in 2022. He finished out that season with St. Louis, recording a 3.77 ERA in 15 games, a glimpse of what was to come. In 2023, he recorded a 3.68 ERA in 27 games. The 2024 season would be his breakout year, with Romero posting a 3.36 ERA in 65 games. He followed that up with a stellar 2.07 ERA in 65 games during the 2025 season. So, over five seasons with St. Louis, Romero had a 3.07 ERA in 216 games. He was a part of the stellar Milwaukee bullpen that dominated in the postseason. In seven playoff appearances, Romero posted a 1.13 ERA. Entering his age-31 season, Romero should be one of the more highly sought-after free agents in this class. With his familiarity in St. Louis, it wouldn’t be surprising at all if the team seeks a reunion. State Of the Team’s Bullpen While the Cardinals desperately need pitching, does it make sense to add during a mini-rebuild? Riley O’Brien is set to be the closer for St. Louis again despite blowing eight saves in 2026. After O’Brien, there isn’t a clear plan for who should be the setup man. Justin Bruihl pitched in a team-high 73 games in 2026, recording a 3.59 ERA. Gordon Graceffo pitched in 62 games with a 2.67 ERA. Both of those arms should be considered for the eighth-inning role. However, Romero has been the more consistent and experienced arm during his career and would fit in rather nicely in the Cardinals bullpen. George Soriano, Max Rajcic, Luis Gastelum, Hancel Rincon, Cade Winquest and Brycen Mautz, among others, will fight for roles in the bullpen. The Cardinals bullpen was one of the worst in baseball, with a 4.51 ERA. If they reunite with Romero, they have a solid chance of improving that number. nigeria.description: The 4-4 draw against Aston Villa felt like a victory at Old Trafford, but the fact that supporters could celebrate a point while their club sits in the relegation zone tells a more troubling story about how far United’s expectations have fallen. There was a time when a draw at Old Trafford felt like a defeat. Manchester United were a club built around winning, where anything short of three points could leave supporters disappointed, regardless of the performance. The expectation was not simply to compete but to dominate, to set the standards and to make winning feel like an obligation. Those expectations seem increasingly distant. On Sunday, Manchester United celebrated a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa with the sort of emotion usually reserved for a significant victory. Two goals in stoppage time, courtesy of Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu, rescued a point after Michael Carrick’s side had twice fallen two goals behind. The comeback was extraordinary, the atmosphere was electric and the players had every reason to appreciate their resilience. But perhaps the most revealing aspect of the afternoon was not the comeback itself. It was how much it meant. Manchester United are now in a position where avoiding defeat feels like an achievement. A point against Aston Villa, under ordinary circumstances, would hardly have been considered a successful afternoon for a club of United’s stature. Yet the circumstances have become so desperate that the draw felt like a victory. That is how quickly footballing standards can collapse. United sit 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 matches . They have managed just one league victory, recorded against Ipswich Town in August, and Sunday’s result extended their winless league run to eight matches. It is a club-record sequence in the Premier League. The numbers are alarming, but the deeper concern is what they reveal about the club’s changing relationship with success. Manchester United have become a team defined by what they are trying to avoid rather than what they are trying to achieve. Instead of discussing title challenges, European qualification or the development of a convincing footballing identity, the conversation increasingly revolves around managerial uncertainty, defensive mistakes, relegation calculations and the possibility of another disappointing weekend. Survival has become the immediate ambition. And that is a remarkable development for a club whose history was built on refusing to accept anything less than excellence. There was the determination to fight back, the willingness to keep attacking and the refusal to surrender even when the game appeared beyond them. nigeria.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
nigeria.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days. nigeria.title: Full list: Canada lists foreigners eligible for rural permanent residence
nigeria.description: Canada has outlined six eligibility requirements for foreign nationals seeking permanent residence through its Rural Community Immigration Program, a pathway designed to attract skilled immigrants to participating rural communities across the country. The programme offers permanent residence to eligible foreigners who want to work and settle in selected Canadian communities, particularly areas seeking skilled migrants to fill positions that cannot be filled by local residents. According to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), participating communities will approve designated employers to recruit skilled foreign nationals for available positions. To qualify for permanent residence under the programme, applicants must obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community and secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within that community. They must also have at least one year, equivalent to 1,560 hours, of related work experience within the previous three years. Other requirements include demonstrating language proficiency through an approved test, possessing a Canadian educational credential or its foreign equivalent, and providing proof of sufficient funds to support themselves and their families. Full list of eligibility requirements According to IRCC, foreigners seeking permanent residence through the programme must meet the following six requirements: Community recommendation: Obtain a valid recommendation certificate from a participating community in Canada. Valid job offer: Secure a valid job offer from a designated employer within the participating community. Work experience: Have at least one year (1,560 hours) of related work experience within the past three years. Language proficiency: Demonstrate English or French language ability by taking an approved language test. Educational qualification: Possess a Canadian educational credential or a foreign equivalent. Proof of funds: Provide evidence of having sufficient money to support themselves and their families after arriving in Canada. The programme is designed to help participating rural communities attract skilled foreign nationals while providing immigrants with an opportunity to obtain permanent residence and establish themselves in Canada. Applicants are required to satisfy the eligibility conditions and secure the necessary community recommendation and employment offer before applying for permanent residence. The decision followed BON’s 82nd General Assembly in Calabar, Cross River State, where the organisation raised concerns about the sustainability of broadcast operations amid mounting economic challenges. In a statement issued on Monday night by the Minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, Idris said the suspension was part of efforts by the Federal Government to create a more conducive operating environment for broadcasters. “Any increase in licence fees is hereby put on hold. All reviews relating to licences are suspended until further notice. I am directing the NBC to ensure strict compliance while we review the situation,” he said. The minister also directed the Director-General of the National Broadcasting Commission (NBC) to expedite the review of the National Broadcasting Code to ensure that its provisions reflect current developments and emerging realities in the industry. On the Digital Switch-Over (DSO) programme, Idris promised to convene a stakeholders’ meeting to address outstanding concerns and resolve challenges affecting its implementation. He further disclosed that he had directed the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON) to ensure full enforcement of the 45-day payment period for advertising services, following BON’s request for improved compliance with the policy. The minister also assured the delegation that the ministry would engage relevant stakeholders on concerns surrounding access to affordable financing and spectrum allocation. Describing broadcasting as critical to national development, Idris said the industry played an important role in strengthening democracy, promoting national cohesion and ensuring public access to credible and accurate information. With the 2027 general elections approaching, he urged broadcasters to uphold professionalism, fairness and ethical standards in their reportage. “Freedom of expression must go with responsibility. You cannot simply say anything and claim to be practising journalism. “Journalism has standards, procedures and ethics. I urge broadcasters to ensure that what they report is factual, responsible and promotes national unity and peaceful coexistence,” the minister said. nigeria.title: Turkey Steel Factory Explosion Kills 16, Injures 13
nigeria.description: An explosion ripped through a steel plant in western Turkey on Monday, killing 16 people and injuring 13, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, announcing investigations into the tragedy. Eight workers were trapped at the HABAS steel factory about 60 kilometres (37 miles) north of the port city of Izmir, where the blast struck around midday (0900 GMT), said Izmir governor Suleyman Elban. Footage posted online showed a huge cloud of thick smoke pouring into the sky as flames appeared to engulf a tall structure within the HABAS Demir Celik plant in Aliaga. “The circumstances surrounding this tragic incident, which has deeply saddened our nation, including how and why it happened, whether there was any negligence, and who bears responsibility, will be established,” Erdogan said on television. Turkey’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan talks with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung during their meeting at the presidential Blue House in Seoul on November 3, 2026. Photo by JEON HEON-KYUN / POOL / AFP He said two of the injured were in serious condition. HABAS is a privately owned group and one of Turkey’s top steel producers. Crane Collapse According to Izmir’s governor, the blast was caused by an overhead crane that collapsed into a large industrial furnace used during the liquid steel casting process. “While a boiler replacement operation was being carried out at the HABAS iron and steel factory, the overhead crane fell and landed in the arc furnace, causing an explosion in the steel mill behind it,” Elban told reporters, referring to a large electric-powered steelmaking furnace. An eyewitness, Deniz Ulker, said it felt like an “earthquake”. “When I looked at the factory across the street, thick black smoke was coming out. A fire broke out where the chimney was,” Ulker told Anadolu news agency. “It was like a bomb going off,” said Turan Ilbay, who works as a truck driver at the factory and also spoke to Anadolu. Izmir mayor Cemil Tugay said on X that rescue teams were “continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform” and that those affected were factory workers. Safety Issues Workers’ groups said there was a long record of safety issues at HABAS. Contacted by an AFP journalist, HABAS declined to answer questions. Before Monday’s explosion, the Evrensel daily said at least 11 workers had died over the past decade while working there. Turkey’s Labour Party, a small Marxist faction, said on X it was the third time in three weeks that workers had lost their lives at HABAS. The gathering, held in Ikeja on Saturday, November 7, 2026, was themed, “One Community, One Future: Building the Next Generation of Traders.” The event featured discussions on financial market education, trading opportunities and the future of the trading industry in Africa. Speaking at the event, Wilfred Obasi, Regional Director for Africa at TenTrade, identified impatience and the desire to make quick money as major challenges confronting young traders. “For young traders, they are not patient enough. People want to make quick money. It is why we are making the event work today to enlighten young traders,” Obasi said. He explained that the event was organised to expose young people to the realities of financial trading and help them develop the patience and knowledge required to navigate the market. He identified fear, greed, fear of missing out (FOMO) and revenge trading as common emotional traps that could undermine trading decisions and expose traders to losses. Adeagbo stressed that traders must develop the discipline to manage risks and avoid making decisions based on emotions. Similarly, Kehinde Shogeke, TenTrade’s Sales Team Lead, said traders needed adequate market knowledge, sufficient capital and discipline to improve their chances of navigating the financial markets. He observed that many people entered forex trading without understanding its fundamentals, viewing it instead as an opportunity to make quick money. “Most traders or new traders see forex as a get-rich-quickly scheme. There is a basic knowledge of the market that they must have. Have a good knowledge, capital and discipline,” he said. nigeria.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Members and supporters of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Nasarawa State on Monday staged a protest in Lafia over alleged political violence, intimidation of party members and the disruption of the party’s presidential rally attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima. Addressing journalists and security officials during the demonstration, the state APC Chairman, Dr. Aliyu Bello, called for investigations into reported attacks on party supporters, including the alleged killing of a supporter in the Tudun Wada area of Lafia. Bello expressed concern over what he described as the failure of law enforcement agencies to act on complaints previously submitted by the party. He said the protest was organised to demand justice and adequate protection for party members, insisting that the APC remained committed to peaceful political activities. “We came here to demand justice that a full-scale investigation be carried out and the perpetrators of these acts arrested and prosecuted,” he said. The APC chairman also raised concerns about alleged threats and conduct by some opposition figures, calling on security agencies to ensure that all political actors operate within the law. Responding on behalf of Governor Abdullahi Sule, the Deputy Governor, Dr Emmanuel Akabe, described the reported incidents as a matter of concern and criticised the security arrangements surrounding the disruption of the Vice-President’s rally. Akabe said security agencies had been briefed ahead of Shettima’s visit and stressed that protecting lives and property remained their responsibility. “It is unfortunate because the responsibility of security men is to protect lives and property. If you cannot protect individuals in your state, then a lot needs to be answered,” he said. The deputy governor disclosed that the State Emergency Security Council had convened to consider measures to prevent further disturbances. He assured the protesters that the state government would support efforts to ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. Speaking on behalf of the Nasarawa State Police Command, Assistant Commissioner of Police Gaya Ahmed reaffirmed the neutrality of security agencies and their commitment to investigating complaints. “The IGP has made it clear that the police are neutral, and we keep on maintaining that neutrality,” Ahmed said. He assured the protesters that petitions submitted by the APC would be forwarded to the incoming Commissioner of Police for investigation. A representative of the Department of State Services (DSS), the Deputy Director of Administration, also acknowledged receipt of the party’s complaints and commended the protesters for conducting themselves peacefully without obstructing public roads. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide Amundi, Europe’s largest asset manager, raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by about 44% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 6 shows, lifting the position to 1,903,725 shares worth $291.4 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager. The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. MSTR roughly doubled during the third quarter itself. The June 30 13F valued Amundi’s then-smaller stake at an implied $86.93 a share, against the $153.09 Sept. 30 close, so the dollar value of the position rose faster than the share count. Since then the stock has tracked bitcoin’s slide into the mid-$70,000s, wiping out a large share of that mark-to-market gain for anyone still holding the Sept. 30 position. The timing matters because Strategy funds most of its bitcoin buys by selling new MSTR common under an at-the-market program. A weaker share price raises more dilution for every coin purchased, which is the feedback loop that has defined the stock’s moves this year. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine North Korea Is Minting Its Own Meme Coins to Launder Binance Hack Loot North Korean launderers are creating their own worthless meme coins and pushing stolen Binance funds through them so the coins never move directly from one wallet to another, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said Monday. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the operators minted at least six new tokens on the NEAR blockchain — named FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU — paired each with NEAR in its own liquidity pool, then bought the tokens with stolen NEAR and sold them back out through a second set of wallets. About 117,000 NEAR, or roughly $430,000, passed through the six tokens, Elliptic wrote . The trail sits inside the broader laundering of the Oct. 29 Binance theft, which the exchange has put at $6.34 billion and which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. sports.title: Jupiter swimming and diving wins first-ever state championship
sports.description: Jupiter boys swimming and diving has completed its "dream" season with the most coveted of state hardware. The Warriors' program won its first-ever state championship, pacing the pool across Class 4A to finish first at the podium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Jupiter outlasted runner-up Cypress Bay by 5.5 points to take home gold, with the competition coming down to the very last event. The Warriors team swam the 400 yard relay with a time of 3:01.30, edging the second-place Lightning in the event as well as the total team score. "It was an incredible, historical moment for Jupiter High School because this is the first time we're winning the championship title with the boys," head coach Kiril Zahariev said. Jupiter paced the field with 206.5 points, followed by Cypress Bay with 201, Winter Park with 186.5, Nease with 153, and Riverview Sarasota with 143 to round out Florida's top five across Class 4A. FHSAA football playoff bracket release: 5 Palm Beach County takeaways Wellington transfer Julian Granison and Charles "Buddy" Howard shared the honors of "MBS" as Zahariev puts it ― "most valuable swimmer." Granison, a Florida commit, won the 50-yard (19.50, a personal best) and 100-yard frees (42.86, a personal best) events, while Howard, a Michigan commit, took first place in the 200-yard free (1:36.70, a personal best) and 100-yard fly (48.15) events. Chase Young and Asher Smith also participated in the winning 400-yard free relay team, while Slater Woodard helped the Warriors win the 200 free relay. The Warriors boys program boasted six seniors this season, with all coming together to finish their respective high school careers on top with the state title. "It was an amazing performance by all the kids," Zahariev said. "We are so blessed with the title." On the Jupiter girls' side, NC State commit Veronica Metz won the 200 free in a time of 1:45.68, helping the Warriors to a fourth-place finish. Boca Raton junior Caleb Caponera also shined for the Bobcats' boys program with two titles. He swam a 1:46.57 in the 200 IM and a 55.71 in the 100 breast. sports.title: St. Louis Cardinals Interested in Reunion With World Series Champion
sports.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - JULY 6: Oliver Marmol #37 of the St. Louis Cardinals looks on prior to the game against the Miami Marlins at loanDepot park on July 6, 2023 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Sam Navarro/Getty Images) Getty The St. Louis Cardinals traded away starter Dustin May and reliever JoJo Romero to the Milwaukee Brewers at the Trade Deadline in a fire sale. Those two players would win a World Series with Milwaukee, becoming key contributors. Now, both will hit free agency. May’s market is likely cold after how he finished the year, but Romero’s could be hot. According to Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Dispatch, the Cardinals are considering a reunion with Romero. The left-handed reliever recorded a 3.36 ERA in 2026 between St. Louis and Milwaukee. Should The Cardinals Bring Back Romero? The Philadelphia Phillies drafted Romero in the fourth round of the 2016 MLB Draft out of Yavapai College. He debuted with Philadelphia during the COVID-shortened 2020 season with horrible results. In 25 games over three seasons with the Phillies, Romero recorded a 7.89 ERA. Philadelphia traded him to St. Louis in exchange for utility man Edmundo Sosa in 2022. He finished out that season with St. Louis, recording a 3.77 ERA in 15 games, a glimpse of what was to come. In 2023, he recorded a 3.68 ERA in 27 games. The 2024 season would be his breakout year, with Romero posting a 3.36 ERA in 65 games. He followed that up with a stellar 2.07 ERA in 65 games during the 2025 season. So, over five seasons with St. Louis, Romero had a 3.07 ERA in 216 games. He was a part of the stellar Milwaukee bullpen that dominated in the postseason. In seven playoff appearances, Romero posted a 1.13 ERA. Entering his age-31 season, Romero should be one of the more highly sought-after free agents in this class. With his familiarity in St. Louis, it wouldn’t be surprising at all if the team seeks a reunion. State Of the Team’s Bullpen While the Cardinals desperately need pitching, does it make sense to add during a mini-rebuild? Riley O’Brien is set to be the closer for St. Louis again despite blowing eight saves in 2026. After O’Brien, there isn’t a clear plan for who should be the setup man. Justin Bruihl pitched in a team-high 73 games in 2026, recording a 3.59 ERA. Gordon Graceffo pitched in 62 games with a 2.67 ERA. Both of those arms should be considered for the eighth-inning role. However, Romero has been the more consistent and experienced arm during his career and would fit in rather nicely in the Cardinals bullpen. George Soriano, Max Rajcic, Luis Gastelum, Hancel Rincon, Cade Winquest and Brycen Mautz, among others, will fight for roles in the bullpen. The Cardinals bullpen was one of the worst in baseball, with a 4.51 ERA. If they reunite with Romero, they have a solid chance of improving that number. technology.title: Attackers backdoor trusted AWS integrations to steal secrets
technology.description: Unknown attackers used compromised identity and access management (IAM) credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account to access customer AWS environments, stealing secrets and other sensitive data from S3 buckets. Qubole is a cloud data processing platform that uses cross-account IAM roles to manage compute and access storage in customers' AWS environments without requiring customers to provide long-lived AWS access keys. The supply-chain attack abused this third-party, cross-account trust relationship. Google’s cloud-security shop Wiz declined to tell us how many organizations were affected, but called it a “broad, opportunistic supply chain campaign” that hit “multiple” customer environments. “Because many organizations left trust policies active even after deprecating the platform, the attacker was able to successfully assume integration roles, enumerate cloud resources, harvest secrets, and siphon data,” the researchers told The Register in an emailed response to questions. Neither AWS nor Qubole responded to The Register 's inquiries. Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders after AI data security company Sentra flagged suspicious activity, traced the malicious activity back to October 14, when credentials associated with Qubole's AWS account were used to call the sts:AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for customer-managed integration roles. The calls originated from Qubole AWS account 805246085872 , and used IAM user ID AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS , Wiz analysts Zack Morrow, Sean Johnstone, and Benjamin Read said in a Monday blog about the supply chain attack. “Across the affected environments, Wiz CIRT has not observed this IAM user in any activity other than that associated with this threat actor,” the trio wrote. This activity continued on October 15, and on October 18, the digital intruders began using a second IAM user from the same account. Once inside customers’ environments, the crooks began probing a ton of AWS services and stealing credentials, keys, and other secrets stored across Lambda, Secrets Manager, and SSM Parameter Store. The miscreants also used TruffleHog to test AWS credentials belonging to victim organizations, discover their Microsoft Entra ID secrets, and request OAuth tokens using Okta client credentials also uncovered while snooping around the AWS environments. Abusing the integration roles also allowed the criminals to steal data from customers’ S3 storage, although it seems they were largely opportunistic attackers, in some cases downloading entire buckets, as opposed to state-sponsored spies looking for specific data. The threat hunters haven’t attributed the supply chain attack to any particular group, and say they don’t have any insight into how the miscreants are using the stolen data. While investigating this incident, Wiz spotted a separate campaign between October 8 and October 11 that also used customer-owned AWS access keys for Qubole integrations. science.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
science.description: null Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium. Now, researchers have used JWST data to test whether one particular Little Red Dot, known as blackAbell 2744-QSO1 (QSO1), could host a primordial black hole. "A black hole is an object born from the gravitational death of a star. Primordial black holes are a very different story," study team member Valerio De Luca, of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Johns Hopkins University (JHU) in Maryland, said in a statement . "They come from the physics of the early universe that predates the first stars, when the universe was expanding exponentially in time and space. So the mechanisms for creating primordial black holes are different," De Luca added. Little Red Dots could be the smoking gun of primordial black holes Though scientists have theorized about the existence of primordial black holes since they were first proposed by Stephen Hawking in the 1970s, no hard evidence has presented itself. One of the issues scientists have puzzled over is how to tell the difference between a primordial black hole and a "traditional" or astrophysical black hole formed from the supernova death and collapse of a massive star. "Little Red Dots could surround astrophysical black holes, and most probably many of them do, but they could also be primordial black holes, if primordial black holes exist," De Luca said. "So the question becomes, Which ones are primordial and how can we tell?" De Luca and colleagues turned their attention to QS01, located around 13.1 billion light-years from Earth, which is seen as it was just 700 million years after the Big Bang. What makes this Little Red Dot stand out is the fact that it is almost entirely composed of hydrogen and helium. Because these were the universe's first elements, it could be more unspoiled and primordial than other Little Red Dots. The team modeled how a Little Red Dot like QS01 could form from a primordial black hole. That was necessary because the circumstances under which this could happen would have to be very specific. "There are constraints on primordial black holes from cosmological observations," said team member Loris Del Grosso, also of JHU's Department of Physics and Astronomy. The Chandra data shows X-ray point sources represented in purple, and the SDSS data shows the galaxy and foreground and background objects in red and blue. The luminous blue variable and supernova impostor AT 2016blu is in the middle of the small square. X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds Using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory, astronomers have discovered what is triggering repeated outbursts from a giant, unstable star. A new study , published Monday in the latest issue of The Astrophysical Journal, details the discovery of a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another. This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star. This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars. It is also the first of these objects found with a black hole or neutron star companion. The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth. Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun. “For 15 years, astronomers have been watching this star get really bright and then dim again on a regular basis,” said Mojgan Aghakhanloo of the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, who led this study. “Until we were able to get Chandra data at the right time, we couldn’t figure out what was making this happen.” The star AT 2016blu is a type of luminous blue variable, which are hot, massive stars characterized by changes in brightness. Eta Carinae, for example, is a particularly well-known luminous blue variable.) AT 2016blu is a special type of luminous blue variable that undergoes rapid and repeated increases in brightness. The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions, where a massive star collapses onto itself and material then hurtles outward into space. However, unlike in a supernova explosion, the star is not destroyed, so AT 2016blu is also referred to as a “supernova impostor.” Between 2012 and 2026, astronomers detected at least 27 bursts of optical light, or light in wavelengths that are visible to our eyes, from AT 2016blu roughly every 113 days. “This star’s behavior was confusing at first because it kept acting like a supernova, but clearly it’s not because it keeps surviving these outbursts about three times a year,” said co-author Núria Torres-Albà, also of the University of Virginia. “To understand the cause of these eruptions, we realized we needed X-ray data, timed so that we’d observe the star when it was in an outburst.” The team used Chandra because it is the only X-ray telescope with sharp enough vision to distinguish AT 2016blu

science.title: Starfish Space loses contact with 1st 'Otter' servicing spacecraft, ending NASA tech-demo mission
science.description: null Starfish Space's first Otter has died, just a month after it reached the final frontier. The Seattle startup announced on Tuesday (Nov. 3) that its Otter 24C satellite suffered a glitch in low Earth orbit (LEO) and is not recoverable. The anomaly killed an ambitious mission in the cradle, as Otter 24C was still in the commissioning phase. Otter 24C launched Oct. 1 on SpaceX 's Transporter-18 mission, a rideshare flight that carried a total of 130 payloads to LEO (including a prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher , Google's planned AI constellation). The Starfish satellite was flying a mission for NASA called Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability, or SSPICY for short. The goal was to "demonstrate technologies necessary for future debris-removal missions as well as for future applications in the servicing and inspection of active spacecraft," according to NASA's SSPICY site . "This advances NASA's in-space manufacturing and assembly (ISAM) goals to ensure a sustainable space operating environment and builds towards a future where objects can be assembled, repaired and maintained in space, significantly expanding possibilities for science and human exploration," the agency added. Starfish Space was a natural partner. The Seattle company plans to become a big player in the nascent field of satellite servicing , using its line of Otter craft to repair, refuel or deorbit other satellites for a variety of customers. Illustration of a Starfish Space Otter satellite rendesvousing with another spacecraft in Earth orbit. (Image credit: Starfish Space) SSPICY marked Otter's spaceflight debut. The mission plan called for the 739-pound (335-kilogram) Otter 24C spacecraft to approach and inspect "up to four inoperable space objects of U.S. origin" over the course of a two-year mission, performing detailed visual inspections. But Otter 24C never got the chance to perform any of these orbital rendezvous. "While working through commissioning steps, Starfish eventually stopped receiving data from Otter 24C," the company said in a Nov. 3 X post . "An investigation into the loss of communications has determined that fault protection on the satellite bus provided by [California company] Astro Digital had an error that turned off the radio and prevented re-establishing communications," Starfish added. "Starfish, NASA, and Astro Digital have concluded that Otter 24C is not recoverable." The company further said that it's implementing fixes to reduce the chances that the problem will crop up in the future. And it stressed that Otter 24C's death will not be in vain. "The work completed through Otter 24C will directly contribute to the success of future Otter missions, as Starfish continues developing the technologies and operations required to make satellite servicing a routine capability in orbit," Starfish said. science.title: NASA just launched a $1 million Moon Base Student Challenge to award cash prizes to students that solve lunar base problems
science.description: null CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — NASA has officially launched the Moon Base Student Challenge, asking students to help build humanity's future on the moon. And there's $1 million in prizes up for grabs for the winners. To build and sustain a base on the moon , NASA will have to solve a myriad of problems. And they're looking to the next generation for help, the space agency's chief Jared Isaacman said Sunday (Nov. 8). "We are inviting students from across the country to help solve some of the problems that stand between humanity and a permanent presence on another world," Isaacman said. "We're putting 1 million in prizes together to support the best ideas and recognize the teams behind them." Isaacman made this announcement wearing his blue flight suit from the rocket garden at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center amidst the agency's MAX POWER air show event . Just the day before, he flew fighter jets in that suit and even jumped out of a plane, skydiving into the event. Soon after this announcement, he was flying another fighter plane above the crowd. The audience for this announcement was filled with students of all ages. Some young children wearing costume spacesuits squeezed as close as they could to the front of the room while teenagers considering their futures listened intently. It was clear that Isaacman's presence and words were landing with this group. But what moon base challenges does NASA want to see these students tackle? In short, all of them. "The moon base will allow us to conduct groundbreaking science, test new technologies, and prepare again for where we inevitably go next, which is the red planet," he said. "But before any of that can happen, we have an awful lot of problems that need to be solved." "We need ways to generate power through the long lunar night . We need to protect our astronauts from that incredibly harsh and dangerous and demanding environment on the surface. We need to move people and equipment around on the surface and support human life three days away from Earth," Isaacman said, illustrating just a few of the big issues that present with the concept of a moon base. NASA Adminisrator Jared Isaacman invites students to help NASA build a moon base at NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Center. (Image credit: Chelsea Gohd) How will it work? This challenge is open to high school and post-secondary students based in the U.S. For participating students, they will form teams that will work on an idea from one of six different technical topics related to creating and running a moon base. These six topics include power systems, habitats, communications, mobility, life support and astronaut safety . science.title: Netflix announces 'Stranger Things' spin-off 'Other Worlds', and it's already teasing a trip to Area 51 (video)
science.description: null So, you thought "Stranger Things" was done and dusted after all that Conformity Gate nonsense? No way! Netflix's sci-fi sensation returns in the live-action prequel series "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure." Created by the Duffer Brothers and Kate Trefry, with the episodes set to be directed by Joe Wright ("Darkest Hour", "Black Mirror"), this new show isn't set in Hawkins or the electric '80s. No, this time around, the action takes place in Marion, Nevada, in 1955, and you know what else is located in Nevada, right? Area 51 . The teaser trailer certainly teases the possibility of a trip to the world's most paradoxically famous secret military base, showcasing a bike and radio resting outside of a fence with a sign that clearly says it's a restricted area (in any TV show or film, that's actually an invitation to see what's on the other side). Of course, the tease doesn't end there, as the thunder booms in the sky and there's a visual hint of a wormhole. No story details about "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" have been released to date, but there are some clues out there for all the Internet sleuths. Trefrey wrote the Henry Creel-focused "Stranger Things: The First Shadow" play, while Matt Duffer explained to Variety how a spin-off show would tackle the rock that Henry found in the briefcase in "Stranger Things." So, yes, expect this to be a Henry-centric affair and the start of his long, hard road to hell and becoming Vecna. (Image credit: Netflix) What'll be interesting, though, is to see how the show ties into the history of Area 51. After all, it was on April 12, 1955, that CIA officer Richard Bissell discovered the site, while the "Other Worlds" trailer has the date of April 19th clearly marked onscreen, so the timelines align nicely here. "Stranger Things" has never been shy of tying itself to real-world science and historical events, so it'll be fascinating to see how the show explores Area 51 as a concept and the secrets everybody believes are hidden there. Was it really a site to test highly advanced weapons and aircraft, or was E.T. 's cousin held hostage there until he revealed Colonel Sanders' 11 herbs and spices? Who knows, with all this renewed excitement around this mysterious military facility, we might get another "Storm Area 51" event to enjoy and laugh at all over again. Regardless, more "Stranger Things" is welcome news, and since it's presumably about one of the show's best characters, Henry Creel, it only adds another layer to his already intriguing lore. If we can't have an origin story about Hopper's incredible and envious moustache, this is the next best thing. "Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure" arrives on Netflix in 2028. science.title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Completes Powered Earth Flybys, Now En Route to Mars
science.description: NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft have each successfully completed a powered Earth flyby, using Earth’s gravity in combination with a sustained engine burn to slingshot themselves toward Mars. With these successful maneuvers complete, the twin spacecraft are on target to reach the Red Planet in September 2027. “This is the first time NASA has used a powered Earth flyby to propel a spacecraft toward Mars, and we’ve now executed this maneuver twice, flawlessly, in just two days,” said Asal Naseri, acting associate flight director for the Heliophysics Division at NASA Headquarters in Washington. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video In November 2026, each of NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft executed a powered flyby of Earth, combining Earth’s gravity with an engine burn, to slingshot itself toward Mars. The first spacecraft made its closest approach around 5 a.m. EST on Saturday, Nov. 7, and the second did so two days later, around 6 a.m. EST on Monday, Nov. 9. In this animation, each spacecraft’s approximately 9-minute trans-Mars injection burn appears as an orange arc along the spacecraft’s trajectory. Advanced Space/Matt Bolliger The two ESCAPADE spacecraft launched from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Nov. 13, 2025, when Earth and Mars were on opposite sides of the Sun. So instead of heading straight for the Red Planet, as most other Mars missions have done, both spacecraft entered a “loiter” or “Earth-proximity” orbit. They charted a first-of-its-kind, kidney-bean-shaped course around a place in space about a million miles from Earth called Lagrange point 2, which is a gravitational balancing point on the opposite side of Earth from the Sun. Then they headed back toward Earth to perform this gravitational slingshot maneuver around our planet once Earth and Mars were favorably aligned. To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The ESCAPADE mission is pioneering a unique path to get to Mars. After launch in November 2025, the two ESCAPADE spacecraft looped around the Earth-Sun Lagrange point 2 (L2), in an “Earth-proximity” or “loiter” orbit that allowed the spacecraft to return to Earth in November 2026 and use our planet’s gravity to slingshot themselves to Mars. science.description: null SpaceX will make spaceflight history this week, if all goes according to plan. The company announced over the weekend that it's targeting Friday (Nov. 13) for the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket, which will attempt something that's never been done before. "The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch," SpaceX wrote in a description of Flight 15 . "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket." SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 14th test flight on Sept. 28, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Super Heavy is Starship's giant booster, and Starship (or Ship for short) is its upper-stage spacecraft. As SpaceX's description noted, both elements are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable. "Catch" refers to SpaceX's recovery mechanism for both stages: Each will return to the launch mount at SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas and be plucked out of the sky by the tower's "chopstick" arms. SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three Starship flights to date, but it has never tried the maneuver with Ship. It's a taller order; Ship flies higher and farther than Super Heavy, so its return to Earth is more complex and energetic.
